entities.summary:
The Argentine Football Association (AFA), founded on February 21, 1893, in Buenos Aires, serves as the foremost governing body of football in Argentina and is pivotal in the development of the sport at both national and international levels. As the oldest football association in South America, AFA has played a critical role in shaping not only Argentine football culture but also the broader landscape of global football, influencing how the game is played and organized. Key figures in its history include presidents such as Julio Grondona, who led the association for over 30 years and was instrumental in expanding the influence of Argentine football worldwide.

Throughout its history, AFA has witnessed significant events, including the establishment of the Primera División, Argentina's top professional football league, which began in 1891, just two years prior to AFA's foundation. The association also oversaw the national team's triumphs in international competitions, such as the FIFA World Cup victories in 1978 and 1986, which not only elevated Argentina's status in world football but also infused national pride among its citizens. Furthermore, AFA has been crucial in the organization of domestic tournaments and the promotion of young talent, fostering a competitive environment that has produced legendary players like Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi.
